Check this box if:

The Group Type is Regular Shares or IRA Regular Shares and dividends are paid at quarterly intervals other than normal calendar quarter-ends (March 31, June 30, September 30, December 31), or annually other than at calendar year-end (December 31). For example, a Christmas Club account which pays dividends annually on October 31.

The Group Type is Certificates or IRA Certificates and dividend intervals are based on the account open date versus a calendar month-end. For example, for a certificate opened on January 15 receiving dividends monthly, the first dividend payment will be paid February 15 rather than January 31 (Calendar method).

Select when dividends are calculated and accrued for this product.

If dividends are calculated based on daily compounding select "Daily", else select the Div Calculate Freq  matching the Div Pay Frequency.

If dividends are not due to be posted at the end of a month, all dividends earned through month-end will be calculated, expensed, and posted to the specified Accrual Acct # and held as a future payable until posted to the member accounts.
column24:
If the Group Type is Regular Shares, IRA Shares, or Share Drafts the valid options are:

- AvgDaily: Dividend is calculated using the average balance in the account for the dividend period. 

- DayIn/DayOut: Dividend is calculated on the account balance for each day in the dividend period, then summed to determine the dividend .

- No Dividend
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If the Group Type is Certificates or IRA Certificates the valid options are:

- Simple: Dividend is calculated using the current account balance for the number of days since dividends were last paid (accrued).

- Compound: Dividend is calculated using the balance plus accrued dividends each day.  The Div Calculate Freq must be specified as Daily (Column U).  The dividends compound because accrued dividends are included in the balance calculation.  Used with CD and IRAC Group Types.

- No Dividend
column25:
If dividends for this product are posted less frequently than monthly, select a dividend recalculation method for this product type. This option is only used with Group Type Regular Shares, IRA Shares, or Share Drafts.

No Re-Calc: Do not recalculate dividends which have already been expensed/accrued during the current dividend period.

Re-Calc: Recalculate previous dividends which have been expensed/accrued during the current dividend period using the current dividend rate(s) in the product record. For example, if dividends are posted quarterly and the rate for the first two months of the dividend period was 5%, and the current rate in   the product record is 6% when dividends are calculated for the third month, then the first two months dividends would be recalculated at 6% prior to  posting dividends for the quarter.

Re-Calc Freq: If Div Calculate Method is AvgDaily, recalculate previous dividends which have been expensed/accrued during the current period using the current dividend rate(s) in the product record. This option is used if the credit union wants to calculate dividends based on the average balance over the entire period versus each month in the dividend period being calculated independently. For example, for a product posting dividends quarterly, if the average balance in the account during the first two months was $1,000, but during the last month the account balance dropped causing the average balance for the quarter to be $750, the first two months dividends would be recalculated using an average balance of $750.
